name: octave-v1
status: FROZEN at the written time, before any count of the second annotator (FL_NG) existed or was seen; method, predictions and the evaluation script are fixed by the SHA-256 below
honesty: The method was developed AFTER the aggregate failure of the frozen counter on the real scenes was known: the first annotator's (FL_SA) counts had shown, in aggregate only, that 'ours' is often off by a factor of two on one axis (about 60 % of scenes, more often reading half than double; an octave oracle would give about 13 % MAPE). That aggregate description motivated the work. No per-scene human count, per-scene error, label file or label-derived table of the 76 / 150 real scenes was read (the forbidden paths of the job brief were never opened or listed), and nothing was tuned per scene; parameters were set only on fresh synthetic renders, the 13 legacy crops with 2019 hand counts, and label-free consistency of the real crops (re-shoot pairs, full/quarter-resolution copies, rotated copies). The real crops and their spectra were looked at to understand the failure mode, without counting yarns by eye.

rule.summary: octave-v1 = frozen 'ours' (imported unchanged) + a per-axis secondary-ridge test that can only DOUBLE a count
steps: Run the frozen counter (counting_frozen_final: preprocess + _estimate_pre 'ours', with methods/conf_model.json for the confidence) on the rectified crop -> counts h, v, lattice angles, weave, confidence; these reproduce methods/predictions_ours_150.csv exactly (checked by assertions).

For each axis with count c (yarns per crop side) and its lattice angle: shear the frozen pre-processed PCA-grey image (working side N <= 1024) so that this yarn family is axis-parallel (of +angle and -angle the one with more projection power at c), average along the yarns in 8 equal bands, cut each band profile into windows of 6 periods (period T = N / c, hop 3 periods, windows with < 90 % valid pixels skipped), compute the Hann-windowed Fourier coefficients of harmonics k = 1, 2, 3 of T, rotate each window so that k = 1 has zero phase, normalise by the sum of the window's three magnitudes and average over all windows -> mean period shape G(phi) = Re sum_k C_k exp(i k phi).

Find the local maxima of G on 360 samples of one period (circular) and their prominences; r2 = prominence of the second-largest maximum / prominence of the largest, set to 0 unless the second maximum lies 0.35 to 0.5 periods from the largest.
If r2 >= 0.15 and 2c <= 0.42 N (the doubled frequency is inside the frozen analysis band), set c = 2c and repeat the test at the new count (at most 2 doublings). Otherwise keep c.
Output h_count, v_count = the (possibly doubled) counts; weave and confidence are the frozen ones.
rule.rationale: The frozen counter returns the dominant period of the image. A yarn-like ridge between every two counted ridges (in the phase-aligned average period shape) is positive evidence that the counted period holds two yarns (paired / basket-like yarns, floats covering two yarns, alternately bright and dark yarns whose dark member still forms a ridge). Absence of a second ridge is not taken as evidence for halving.

data: synthetic A: 300 fresh renders, seeds 990000-990299, cnn/synth.py v2 as shipped
synthetic B: 300 fresh renders, seeds 991000-991299, + 'oxford' (paired ends) / 'oxfordw' (paired picks) weave matrices and more basket 2/2 (dev/gen_synth.py)
synthetic C: 150 fresh renders, seeds 992000-992149, unbalanced plain / twill (density ratio 1.6-2.4; dev/gen_poplin.py), used as a check
13 legacy crops with 2019 hand counts (a1 a2 a4 a5 a6 a8 a10 r2 r3 r4 r6 r7 r8)
label-free consistency on the 150 real crops: 41 same-patch re-shoot pairs (paper/tables/fabric_groups_v2.json), 47 quarter-resolution copies, 51 rotated copies, 27 other copies (manifest)
selection.criteria: no correct count broken on synthetic or legacy; fewer 2x disagreements on real copies and none created; then lowest synthetic MAPE
selection.candidates_tried: C1 spectral half-shift self-similarity; C2 secondary-ridge doubling (CHOSEN, rho 0.05-0.30 scanned, 0.15 frozen); C2b C2 + single-ridge halving; C2c C2 + halving gated by an on-axis half-frequency peak; C3 C2 on PCA-grey + B, G, R channels; C4 harmonic ratio |C2|/|C1|; C5 multi-estimator octave vote; C6 octave-guarded fusion. Numbers: methods/octave/dev/octave_v1_candidates.json

legacy13.note: this pipeline (legacy.rectify_legacy + frozen estimate) gives 9.23% for frozen ours; the paper figure 11.6% uses the legacy13 protocol of methods/results

real150_label_free_consistency.definition: pairs: reshoot = 41 accepted same-patch pairs of scene reps (paper/tables/fabric_groups_v2.json; |angle|<15 same axes, 75-90 swapped, else sorted); res = quarter_res_copy vs rep; rot = members with scene_rot_k != 0 vs rep; copy = png/byte/notebook copies vs rep (manifest). Per axis r = max/min of the two counts; 2x if 1.70 <= r <= 2.35.

expected_effect: octave-v1 changes 4 of the 152 axes of the 76 scene representatives (scenes 35 h, 121 h, 98 v, 124 v: two re-shoot pairs, doubled consistently) and 8 of the 300 file axes. The change in mean scene MAPE against any reference is therefore bounded by about -1.3 points (all four doublings right, frozen APE 50 % on those axes) to +2.6 points (all four wrong). Pre-registered expectation: |dMAPE vs frozen ours| <= 1.5 points; a confidence interval excluding 0 is not expected. The diagnosis (dev/octave_v1_candidates.json) indicates that most octave errors of the frozen counter are systematic and not visible as a resolved second ridge, so an image-evidence octave rule cannot recover most of the oracle gap.

evaluation.script: methods/octave/eval_octave_v1.py (frozen here; SHA-256 above). Tested only on FAKE label files (ours' counts x log-normal noise, filenames containing 'fake').
evaluation.unit: scene = scene representative (scene_id = rep id), all 76 representatives that the reference labels (both h_tpi and v_tpi finite and > 0, 'labelled' truthy)
evaluation.axis_convention: reference h_tpi <-> prediction h_count, v_tpi <-> v_count (paper/tools/score150.py); GPT-6.1-sol P1: h = gpt-6.1-sol__v, v = gpt-6.1-sol__h
evaluation.per_scene: APE_ax = 100 |pred - ref| / ref; scene MAPE = (APE_h + APE_v) / 2; both5 = APE_h <= 5 and APE_v <= 5; missing / non-positive prediction = APE 100 on that axis

primary.reference: second annotator FL_NG alone (per-scene CSV, h_tpi / v_tpi)
outcomes: share of scenes with both axes within +-5 %
primary.inference: paired scene MAPE difference: mean, 95 % percentile CI from a scene bootstrap (10,000 resamples of the scenes with replacement, numpy default_rng(20261012)), two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p (scipy, zero_method='wilcox'); both5 difference in percentage points with the same bootstrap CI and an exact two-sided McNemar p
primary.command: python methods/octave/eval_octave_v1.py --labels <FL_NG scene csv> --reference each --out-json methods/octave/eval_primary_FL_NG.json --out-txt methods/octave/eval_primary_FL_NG.txt
primary.interpretation: octave-v1 is called better (worse) than a comparator only if the 95 % CI of the paired MAPE difference lies entirely below (above) 0; otherwise 'no detectable difference'. Both outcomes and both comparisons are reported whatever their direction.

secondary.reference: mean of the two annotators (FL_NG and FL_SA; per scene and axis, mean of the available counts)
secondary.command: python methods/octave/eval_octave_v1.py --labels <FL_NG scene csv> <FL_SA scene csv> --reference mean --out-json methods/octave/eval_secondary_mean.json

secondary.reference: FL_SA alone - POST HOC: FL_SA's counts revealed the failure mode that motivated octave-v1, so this comparison is not confirmatory
